title: System Design Interview - An insiders guide volume 3

blocks.text: A hash key is a way to organize data. It helps locate data quickly in a system.
The hash function mentioned here is not the same as the one used in a problem called "rehashing." Rehashing is a technique to reassign keys when there's a need to change how data is stored.
This hash function does not use a modular operation. A modular operation usually limits numbers within a range, but this one doesn’t.
Figure 5-6 shows a visual representation of where the cache keys go.
These cache keys are spread out on something called a hash ring.
The hash ring helps quickly find which server holds the data tied to each key.

script:
A hash key is a way to organize data. It helps locate data quickly in a system.

The hash function here is different from what's called rehashing. Rehashing is when you change how keys are assigned as data storage approaches evolve.

This hash function doesn’t involve a modular operation. A modular operation would limit numbers to a specific range, but this function doesn’t do that.

Figure 5-6 shows where the cache keys go. There are four cache keys: key0, key1, key2, and key3. They’re spread out on a hash ring. This ring allows you to quickly find which server holds the data associated with each key.
